summary: Calcium dobesilate is an oral capillary-stabilising (vasoprotective/angioprotective) agent used for diabetic retinopathy, chronic venous insufficiency, and symptomatic relief in haemorrhoidal disease. It reduces increased capillary permeability and fragility, decreases platelet aggregation and blood viscosity. It is NOT FDA-approved; it is licensed in many European, Asian and Latin American countries (SmPC/regional labelling). A recognised, though rare, risk is agranulocytosis.
indications: Chronic venous insufficiency of the lower limbs (oedema, cramps, restless legs)
Symptomatic treatment of acute haemorrhoidal attacks (adjunct)

dosage.d: 500 mg twice or three times daily (commonly 1000-1500 mg/day)

dosage.n: Reduce to maintenance once symptoms improve

dosage.d: 500 mg 2-3 times daily for several days, then reduce
dosage.n: Short course; adjunct to local measures

admin: Take with or after meals to minimise gastrointestinal upset
Use the lowest effective maintenance dose for long-term venous indications
Stop and seek medical advice if fever, sore throat, or mouth ulcers occur (possible agranulocytosis)
moa: Calcium dobesilate acts on the microcirculation to reduce pathologically increased capillary permeability and fragility. It is thought to act on the endothelium and basement membrane, decreasing capillary hyperpermeability, lowering blood and plasma viscosity, reducing platelet aggregation, and improving lymphatic drainage and red-cell flexibility, thereby reducing tissue oedema. Antioxidant effects on the vascular wall have also been proposed.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to calcium dobesilate or excipients
monitor: Full blood count if signs of infection arise during treatment

preg: There are limited data on use in pregnancy; calcium dobesilate is generally avoided, particularly during the first trimester. Use only if the potential benefit clearly justifies any potential risk, in line with regional labelling.
lact: Small amounts are excreted in breast milk. Avoid during breastfeeding, or discontinue nursing, unless considered essential.
renal: Use with caution in renal impairment; dose reduction is advised in significant impairment, and the drug is removed by dialysis (consider timing in dialysis patients).
hepatic: No specific dosage recommendations; use with caution in hepatic impairment.

moderate: May potentiate the effect of antihypertensive or other agents lowering blood viscosity (theoretical)
minor: May interfere with creatinine assays in some laboratory methods
interactions.food: Take with meals to reduce gastrointestinal upset.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause falsely low serum creatinine results with certain (Jaffe/enzymatic) laboratory methods — interpret renal tests with caution.

serious: Agranulocytosis (rare but recognised) — fever, sore throat, infection
emergency: Signs of agranulocytosis with sepsis (high fever, severe sore throat)

monitoring: Full blood count if fever, sore throat, or signs of infection occur
Symptom response (oedema, venous symptoms, retinopathy parameters)
Renal function in patients with impairment
counsel: Take with food to reduce stomach upset
Stop the medicine and contact your doctor at once if you develop fever, sore throat, or mouth ulcers
Tell your laboratory you take this drug, as it can affect some kidney (creatinine) tests
For venous symptoms, also use measures such as leg elevation and compression as advised
This medicine is not approved in all countries — follow your prescriber's instructions
pk: Symptomatic effect develops over days to weeks
Plasma peak ~6 hours after oral dose
Store below 25-30C; protect from moisture (per regional labelling)
pearls: NOT FDA-approved — licensed via EMA member states (SmPC) and many Asian/Latin American countries; this record is based on SmPC/BNF-type sources, not an FDA label
Rare but important risk of agranulocytosis — advise patients to report fever/sore throat and check FBC
Can cause falsely low serum creatinine with some assay methods — flag to the laboratory
Evidence of benefit in diabetic retinopathy and chronic venous insufficiency is modest; used mainly as an adjunct
Removed by dialysis — consider dose timing in dialysis patients
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose. Do not take a double dose.
overdose: Experience is limited; overdose may cause gastrointestinal symptoms. There is no specific antidote — provide supportive and symptomatic care; calcium dobesilate is removed by haemodialysis if needed.
